card.name: Linking words before developmental conditions
card.fires_on: Small linking words (with, has, is, commas, or) right before a named developmental or genetic condition, such as Down's syndrome or autism, in text about children and disabilities.

modes.label: With/has before a condition
modes.description: The word 'with' or 'has' after child, children or son, where a disability is expected next.

modes.label: Comma in a list of conditions
modes.description: A comma after one condition in a list, where another condition such as Down's syndrome comes next.
modes.example: and hearing problems have been on the accessibility radar for a long time, cognitive ones are often ignored. More well-known conditions include autism, Down’s syndrome<<,>> dyscalculia and dyslexia.

modes.label: Introducing an example condition
modes.description: Phrases like 'one example is' or 'in this case,' that lead into a named disorder.
